info.title: API Dropshipper
info.description:
Dropshipper-facing public REST API. Place and confirm orders, browse the catalog, read your shops and track shipment incidences — the same surface the Dropea front-end uses, exposed for your own integrations. Public REST API for Dropea. All endpoints require an API Key Bearer token and are subject to per-key rate limits and permission checks. --- ## Getting started First, **select your market** in the **Server** dropdown (top of the page) — Dropea has one deployment per market (PT / ES / IT) and each has its own host. The snippets below use the **PT** host (the default); if you operate in another market, swap `pt.` for `es.` / `it.`. The snippets below walk a full order from zero. Replace `` with your key and run them top to bottom. **1. Create an API Key** — from the **API Keys** section of your Dropea dashboard. Copy the token (shown once) into the requests below. **2. Confirm who you are** ```bash curl https://pt.public-api.dropea.com/dropshipper/me \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` **3. List your shops** — you need a `store_id` to place an order. It is the `id` field of each shop here. ```bash curl https://pt.public-api.dropea.com/dropshipper/shops \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` **4. Browse products** — each product carries a `variants` array; each variant's `variant_id` is the value you put into the order line items. ```bash curl "https://pt.public-api.dropea.com/dropshipper/products?page=1&limit=20" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` **5. Create the order** — send a unique `Idempotency-Key` so a network retry never double-creates. ```bash curl -X POST https://pt.public-api.dropea.com/dropshipper/orders \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: 1f1c9e2a-7b3e-4f0a-9c2d-9d6f0a8e1b22" \ -d '{ "store_id": 1024, "payment_method": "COD", "line_items": [ { "variant_id": 5567, "quantity": 2, "unit_price": 19.99 } ], "customer_details": { "name": "Ada Lovelace", "email": "ada@example.com", "phone": "+34600123456", "shipping_address": { "first_name": "Ada", "last_name": "Lovelace", "address_line_1": "Calle Mayor 1", "city": "Madrid", "state": "Madrid", "postal_code": "28013", "country": "ES" } } }' ``` Order creation is **synchronous with a 15-second budget** (see *Creating an order* below). On success you get **200** with the full order. If the underlying saga has not settled in time you get **504** with an `operation_id` to poll. **6. Confirm the order** — placement leaves the order in `PENDING`; confirm it to hand it to the supplier. ```bash curl -X POST https://pt.public-api.dropea.com/dropshipper/orders/1001/confirm \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: 7a2b9c3d-4e5f-4a1b-8c2d-3e6f9a0b1c4d" ``` **7. Stay in sync** — subscribe webhooks (recommended; see the **Webhooks** section) to receive `order.created`, `order.status.changed` and `order.cancelled` pushes, or poll the order / operation endpoints. --- ## Request fields Fields whose source is not obvious when building an order request: - **`store_id`** — Sequential shop number. Take it from the `id` field of `GET /dropshipper/shops`. - **`line_items[]`** — array of order line items (one or more). Each item carries `variant_id`, `quantity` and `unit_price`: - **`variant_id`** — sequential variant number. Take it from `products[].variants[].variant_id` of `GET /dropshipper/products`. - **`unit_price`** — price per unit charged to the end customer. See *Pricing rules* below — it is validated, not free-form. - **`carrier`** — Optional carrier code. Valid codes come from `GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`. Omit to use the shop's default carrier. - **`service_type`** — Optional. Valid codes are in `services[].code` of the carrier in `GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`. - **`payment_method`** — One of `COD`, `PAYPAL`, `STRIPE`, `SHOPIFY_PAYMENTS`, `PAID`, `MANUAL`, `OTHER`. Any value of the enum is accepted — there is **no per-market gating**. `COD` and `MANUAL` are treated as cash-on-delivery for commission purposes. - **Phone fields** — `phone` (the full number, e.g. `+34600123456`) is the only required phone field. Optionally you may also send it split into `phone_country` (ISO-2 country, e.g. `ES`), `area_code` (dialing prefix, e.g. `+34`) and `phone_number` (the local subscriber number) — these three are optional. ### Pricing rules `unit_price` is **the price you charge the end customer**, and you set it per line item. It is **not** free-form: order-service validates each line against pricing-service, and a request is rejected with **422 `PRICE_BELOW_WHOLESALE`** if `unit_price` is below the variant's wholesale price. In other words, you may price **at or above** wholesale, never below. For bundle variants the validation runs against the sub-variants' wholesale prices. --- ## Creating an order Order creation runs a distributed saga (stock reservation, pricing, fulfilment routing). The endpoint blocks for up to **15 seconds**: - **Settled in time → 200** with the full created order in `data`. - **Not settled in 15s → 504** with `{ "data": { "operation_id": "...", "status": "pending" } }`. The `operation_id` is **the same value as** your `Idempotency-Key`, so poll with the key you already sent: ```bash curl https://pt.public-api.dropea.com/dropshipper/operations/ \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` The operation `status` is one of `in_progress`, `completed` or `failed`. On `completed` the order is created; on `failed` the order was not created and `failure` explains why. --- ## Order lifecycle An order moves through a status machine. The principal statuses are `DRAFT → PENDING → CONFIRMED → PROCESSING → SHIPPING → FINISH` (plus `ERROR` for anomalies). Each step has a sub-status (e.g. `PROCESSING.PICKING`, `SHIPPING.SHIPPED`, `FINISH.DELIVERED`). | Status | Triggered by | Webhook | |--------|--------------|---------| | `PENDING` | Dropshipper creates the order (`POST /dropshipper/orders`) | `order.created` | | `CONFIRMED` | Dropshipper confirms (`POST /dropshipper/orders/{id}/confirm`) | `order.status.changed` | | `PROCESSING` (`PICKING`) | Supplier starts preparing (`POST /supplier/orders/state/preparing`) | `order.status.changed` | | `PROCESSING` (`PACKED`) | Supplier finishes packing (`POST /supplier/orders/state/prepared`) | `order.status.changed` | | `SHIPPING` | Carrier picks up / transits the shipment | `order.status.changed` | | `FINISH` (`DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, ...) | Carrier delivery or cancellation | `order.status.changed` / `order.cancelled` | Happy-path sequence (dropshipper → supplier → delivery): ```text PENDING order created by the dropshipper | v CONFIRMED dropshipper confirms | v PROCESSING.PICKING supplier starts preparing | v PROCESSING.PACKED supplier finishes packing (carrier hand-off) | v SHIPPING carrier picks up / in transit | v FINISH.DELIVERED delivered (or FINISH.CANCELLED on cancellation) ``` Because the envelope carries no `previous_state`, detect transitions by caching the last `status` / `sub_status` per order and diffing on each `order.status.changed` delivery. ## Authentication Every request must carry your API Key as a Bearer token: ```bash Authorization: Bearer ``` Create the key from the **API Keys** section of your Dropea dashboard. The token is shown **once** at creation — store it securely; it cannot be retrieved again. Keys are validated **offline** (the token is self-contained), so there is no token-introspection round-trip on the hot path. > ⚠️ **Shared devices:** for convenience, the **Authorize** button in this > documentation keeps the key you enter in your browser (localStorage). Do > **not** paste a real API Key on a shared or public computer — use a private > window, or clear the authorization when you finish. --- ## Server — pick your market Dropea runs **one deployment per market**, each with its own host. **Select the market you operate in** from the **Server** dropdown at the top of this page — every "Test request" then targets that host. The available hosts are: | Market | Base URL | |--------|----------| | Portugal (PT) — default | `https://pt.public-api.dropea.com` | | Spain (ES) | `https://es.public-api.dropea.com` | | Italy (IT) | `https://it.public-api.dropea.com` | The API surface and this documentation are **identical across markets** — only the host changes. The `curl` examples below use the **PT** host (the default); if you operate in another market, swap `pt.` for `es.` / `it.`. --- ## Rate limiting You can make up to **60 requests per minute** (the limit depends on your role). The window is **rolling**, not fixed: at any moment the API counts the requests from the **last 60 seconds** — it does NOT reset on the clock minute. As your older requests age past 60 seconds, that capacity frees up again. Every response tells you where you stand: - **`X-RateLimit-Limit`** — your maximum requests per window (60). - **`X-RateLimit-Remaining`** — how many you have left right now. - **`X-RateLimit-Window`** — the window length in seconds (60). If you go over, the API returns **429 Too Many Requests** with a **`Retry-After: 60`** header — wait that many seconds, then retry. --- ## Idempotency Mutating requests (`POST`, `PATCH`, `PUT`, and selected `DELETE` endpoints) **require** an `Idempotency-Key` header so retries never duplicate side effects. Send a unique key per logical operation — a **UUID v4** is recommended; the format must match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,255}`. ```bash Idempotency-Key: 1f1c9e2a-7b3e-4f0a-9c2d-9d6f0a8e1b22 ``` Semantics (keys are retained for **24h**, backed by Redis): | Situation | Result | |-----------|--------| | First request with a key | Processed normally; the response is cached under the key. | | Replay with the **same key + same body** | The cached response is returned with header `Idempotent-Replay: true`. | | Same key, **different body** | **422** — a key may not be reused for a different payload. | | Same key while the first call is **still in flight** | **409** — the original operation has not settled yet. | | Original returned **5xx** | Not cached — you may safely retry with the same key. | `GET` requests are inherently idempotent and ignore the header. --- ## Error format Every error shares the same envelope: ```json { "success": false, "message": "human readable summary", "data": null, "failure": { "type": "ValidationFailure", "message": "detailed cause", "code": null, "httpStatusCode": 400 } } ``` `failure.type` maps to the HTTP status: - `ValidationFailure` → **400** - `UnauthorizedFailure` → **401** - `ForbiddenFailure` → **403** - `NotFoundFailure` → **404** - `ConflictFailure` → **409** - `BusinessFailure` → **422** - (rate limit) → **429** - `ServerFailure` / `DatabaseFailure` → **500** - `NetworkFailure` → **503** - (saga timeout) → **504** Representative examples:
401 — missing or invalid API Key ```json { "success": false, "message": "invalid or missing API key", "data": null, "failure": { "type": "UnauthorizedFailure", "message": "API key is invalid or expired", "code": null, "httpStatusCode": 401 } } ```
403 — key lacks the required permission ```json { "success": false, "message": "permission denied", "data": null, "failure": { "type": "ForbiddenFailure", "message": "API key is not allowed to perform this action", "code": null, "httpStatusCode": 403 } } ```
404 — resource not found ```json { "success": false, "message": "resource not found", "data": null, "failure": { "type": "NotFoundFailure", "message": "order not found", "code": null, "httpStatusCode": 404 } } ```
422 — business rule rejected the request ```json { "success": false, "message": "unit price below wholesale", "data": null, "failure": { "type": "BusinessFailure", "message": "Unit price 5 is below wholesale price 8 for variant ...", "code": "PRICE_BELOW_WHOLESALE", "httpStatusCode": 422 } } ```
429 — rate limit exceeded ```json { "success": false, "message": "rate limit exceeded", "data": null, "failure": { "type": "RateLimitFailure", "message": "too many requests, retry after 60s", "code": null, "httpStatusCode": 429 } } ```

bearerAuth.description:
Long-lived API Key issued by Dropea, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

**How to get one:** sign in to your Dropea dashboard → **Settings → API Keys** → **Create API Key**, pick the scopes you need, and copy the token shown **once** at creation time. If you lose it, regenerate — Dropea does not store the plaintext.

This is **not** your dashboard session token: do not paste anything you see in your browser DevTools. Treat the API Key like a password and keep it server-side.

The required permissions per operation are listed in each endpoint under the `x-dropea-permissions` extension.

IdempotencyKeyHeader.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyHeader.description: Unique key per request (UUID v4 recommended). Generate a fresh value on every call — replaying the same key within 24h returns the cached response with `Idempotent-Replay: true`, which is intended for retry/network failure scenarios, not for normal back-to-back requests.

IdempotencyKeyHeaderOptional.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyHeaderOptional.description: Unique key per request (UUID v4 recommended). Optional on this endpoint — if omitted, the server generates one and echoes it back as the `Idempotency-Key` response header, usable to poll `GET /operations/:operation_id`. If sent, replaying the same key within 24h returns the cached response with `Idempotent-Replay: true`.

Failure.description: Error envelope returned by the API on any non-2xx response.

code.description: Machine-readable business error code, when available (e.g. business rule violations). `null` for generic failures.

BasicFailureResponse.description: Standard failure envelope used by every endpoint.

PaginationMeta.description: Pagination metadata describing the current page of results.

total.description: Total number of items across all pages.

limit.description: Page size requested by the caller (capped server-side).

total_pages.description: Total number of pages given the current `limit`.

Pagination.description:
Standard envelope returned by every paginated list endpoint.
The page items live in `items` and pagination metadata in `pagination`.
Endpoint-specific shapes extend this via `allOf` and override the
`items` array element type (e.g. `Order`, `Product`, `Shop`).

OrderLineItem.description: A single line item inside an Order (response shape). Product/variant names and SKU are resolved server-side at creation time and are read-only for consumers.

ean.description: EAN/UPC code. Leading zeros are NOT preserved.

variant_type.description:
- `SIMPLE` — standard product variant (most common value on reads).
- `DEFAULT` — a standard single variant (synonym of `SIMPLE`).
- `BUNDLE` — variant that contains multiple sub-variants assembled as a bundle.

external_name.description:
Original line item name as it appeared in the source channel. For
Shopify-sourced orders this is the Shopify line_item title; `null`
for orders created through other channels.

OrderLineItemInput.description: Line item payload accepted by create/update order mutations. `variant_id` is the human-readable sequential variant number. Product names and SKU are derived by the server from variant_id — they cannot be set by the caller.

OrderShippingAddress.description:
Shipping address as returned on every order read (create / get / list).
The customer contact fields (`full_name`, `email`, `phone_number`) are
merged into this object on output — there is no separate
`customer_details` on read. Phone is exposed combined (`phone_number`)
and, when available, split into `phone_country` / `area_code` /
`phone_without_prefix` (all `null` when the order was created with a
single combined `phone`).

CustomerDetails.description:
Customer + shipping data accepted when **creating or updating** an order
(request shape). On read the order does NOT echo a nested
`customer_details`; this data is flattened into `shipping_address`
(see `OrderShippingAddress`).

Order.description: Order entity as exposed to external API consumers.

status.description: Top-level lifecycle status. The full mapping (with sub-statuses and descriptions) is exposed by `GET /dropshipper/catalogs/order-statuses`. NOTE: `DELIVERED` top-level is **legacy** — the canonical terminal state is `FINISH` (with `sub_status: DELIVERED`). It is kept in the enum only for historical orders; new orders never reach top-level `DELIVERED`.

sub_status.description: Refines the main `status` with the current step inside it (e.g. `PICKING` while in `PROCESSING`, `OUT_FOR_DELIVERY` while in `SHIPPING`). Required to perform state transitions like `Transition orders to prepared`. The `(status, sub_status)` mapping is documented in `GET /dropshipper/catalogs/order-statuses`.

store_owner_id.description: Human-readable sequential user number of the store owner.

confirmed_at.description: Timestamp when the dropshipper confirmed the order. Absent until the order leaves PENDING.

processing_at.description: Timestamp when the order entered preparation (PROCESSING). Absent until the order leaves CONFIRMED.

delivered_at.description: Delivery timestamp. Absent until the order is marked as delivered.

rejected_at.description: Timestamp when the order was rejected by the recipient/carrier. Absent until the order is rejected.

fulfillment_type.description: Who fulfills the order — `SUPPLIER` when the supplier ships it directly, `DROPEA` when it ships from a Dropea-managed warehouse (FBD).

carrier.description: Shipping carrier code (e.g. CTT, GLS, TIPSA).

service_type.description: Carrier-specific service code (e.g. `EMS` for CTT, `24` for TIPSA, `74` for GLS).

external_order_id.description:
External order id supplied by the integrator at creation time
(typically the order id from a connected storefront like Shopify,
WooCommerce, Tienda Nube, etc.). Stored as-is and echoed back on
every order read so integrators can correlate Dropea orders with
their external system.

pack_ids.description: Product numbers of any BUNDLE line items on the order. Absent when the order contains no bundles.

notes.description:
Order notes, exposing only the public-safe fields. The internal
author fields (`user_id`, `user_role`, `user_full_name`,
`user_email`) are never included. Absent when the order has no notes.

type.description: Note category as emitted by order-service (e.g. internal vs customer-facing).

tax_data_dropshipper.description:
Dropshipper fiscal identity snapshot, supplier-facing (needed by
the supplier to invoice the dropshipper). Absent when the upstream
order carries no tax data.

has_equivalence_surcharge.description: Whether the dropshipper is under the Spanish equivalence surcharge regime (recargo de equivalencia).

order_costs.description:
Narrow, supplier-relevant RAW subset of the order costs — only the
provider tax rate and the fulfillment cost components. Never the
full cost breakdown nor a computed subtotal/total. Absent when the
upstream order carries no costs.

tax_rate_provider.description: VAT rate applied to the provider (supplier) side.

tracking_number.description: Carrier tracking number of the order's latest shipment, derived from the order's tracking snapshot. Always present; `null` when the order has no tracking yet.

tracking_url.description: Public tracking URL for the order's latest shipment. Always present; `null` when the order has no tracking yet.

carrier.description:
Carrier code. The live list of valid codes is obtained from the
**List carriers** endpoint (`GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`).
Each entry includes its available `services[]`.

service_type.description:
Carrier-specific service code. The valid codes are obtained from the
**List carriers** endpoint (`GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`) —
inspect `services[].code` of the chosen carrier. Each carrier has
its own service codes. Examples: `EMS` (CTT), `24` (TIPSA), `74` (GLS).

external_order_id.description:
Optional external reference for the order, typically the order id
from the connected storefront (Shopify, WooCommerce, Tienda Nube,
etc.). Stored verbatim and echoed back on every order read so the
integrator can correlate Dropea orders with their source system.

UpdateOrderInput.description: Partial-update payload for PATCH /dropshipper/orders/{id}. Every field is optional; the server transforms the flattened customer_details into the order-service shipping_address shape and validates line_items for same supplier + same fulfillment type before publishing the saga event.

carrier.description:
Carrier code. The live list of valid codes is obtained from the
**List carriers** endpoint (`GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`).

service_type.description:
Carrier-specific service code. The valid codes are obtained from the
**List carriers** endpoint (`GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`) —
inspect `services[].code` of the chosen carrier.

UpdateCustomerDetails.description: Partial customer details. Every field is optional — send only what needs to change.

UpdateShippingAddress.description: Partial shipping address. Every field is optional.

OrderOperationAsync.description: Async response body returned when a sync order mutation cannot complete within the saga timeout (15s). Clients should poll `/dropshipper/operations/{operation_id}` or `/supplier/operations/{operation_id}` to follow up.

message.example: saga did not complete within the configured timeout

variant_id.description: Human-readable sequential variant number. Same field name and value as the Supplier surface (`SupplierProductVariant.variant_id`) and as `OrderLineItemInput.variant_id` used to create orders.

status.description:
Visibility status of the product on the public surface. Internal
lifecycle states (`PENDING_MODERATION`, `BLOCKED`, `INACTIVE`) are
filtered server-side and never surfaced — public consumers only
see purchasable products.
- `PUBLIC` — listed publicly, every variant available.
- `EXCLUSIVE` — only visible if the caller has an allocation on at least one variant.

owner_id.description: Human-readable sequential user number of the supplier.

store_type.description:
Storefront platform the shop is connected to.
- `SHOPIFY` / `WOOCOMMERCE` — managed integration with the platform.
- `GENERIC` — manually-created shop (no auto-sync).
- `UNKNOWN` — unclassified.

store_owner_id.description: Human-readable sequential user number of the store owner.

status.description: Top-level lifecycle status — same vocabulary as `Order.status`. See `GET /dropshipper/catalogs/order-statuses`. NOTE: `DELIVERED` top-level is **legacy** — the canonical terminal state is `FINISH` (with `sub_status: DELIVERED`); kept only for historical orders.

id.description: Auto-incremental numeric identifier assigned at incidence creation. Stable across the resource lifetime and used as the path parameter when transitioning state via `POST /(dropshipper|admin)/issues/{id}/resolve`.

order_id.description: Sequential numeric order identifier (`order_id`) of the order this incidence belongs to. Omitted when the incidence is not linked to an order.

owner_id.description: Sequential numeric dropshipper identifier (`user_id`) that owns the incidence.

type.description:
Normalized incidence type, derived server-side from the carrier-specific incidence code. The same vocabulary applies across CTT, GLS and TIPSA so integrators do not need carrier-specific dictionaries.

Possible values:
- `ADDRESS_INCORRECT` — the delivery address is wrong or incomplete and the carrier could not deliver.
- `RECIPIENT_ABSENT` — the recipient was not present during the delivery attempt.
- `REFUSED_BY_RECIPIENT` — the recipient refused the package.
- `DAMAGED_PACKAGE` — the package is damaged.
- `LOST_PACKAGE` — the package was declared lost by the carrier.
- `CUSTOMS_ISSUE` — held or stuck at customs.
- `PENDING_AUTHORIZATION` — the carrier needs additional authorization to proceed (e.g. recipient signature).
- `PENDING_DATA` — shipment data missing for the carrier to continue (e.g. phone, address complement).
- `POSSIBLE_RETURN` — the carrier anticipates a return to origin.
- `RETURN_REQUESTED` — return to origin was requested.
- `RETAINED` — package retained somewhere in the carrier network (not customs-related).
- `ADMINISTRATIVE_ISSUE` — carrier-internal administrative issue.
- `DELIVERY_FAILED` — delivery attempt failed without a specific cause.
- `GENERAL_INCIDENCE` — generic incidence when the carrier code does not map to any category above.

status.description:
User workflow over the incidence. Independent of the package operational state (`is_active`).

Allowed transitions: `PENDING -> {MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT, RESOLVED}` once. INFO never transitions; MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT and RESOLVED are final.

Possible values:
- `INFO` — informational; the carrier reported an event that does not require DP action (the carrier resolution matrix offers no options).
- `PENDING` — just created, requires DP action. The only state from which a transition is allowed.
- `MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT` — being handled with the customer outside the API. Final state.
- `RESOLVED` — a concrete resolution was applied. The resolution type lives in `resolution_status` and its payload in `resolution_data`. Final state.

resolution_status.description:
Concrete resolution applied by the DP when `status == RESOLVED`. `null` for INFO/PENDING/MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT.

Each value pairs with a specific `resolution_data` shape:
- `RETRY` — `resolution_data = { date, time_window }`. Retry the delivery.
- `CHANGE_ADDRESS` — `resolution_data = { address: {...} }`. Redirect the package.
- `PICKUP_AT_AGENCY` — `resolution_data = null`. The recipient collects from the carrier agency.
- `RETURN_REQUESTED` — `resolution_data = null`. Return the package to origin.
- `SOLUTION_PROVIDED` — `resolution_data = null`. Free-text solution (aportar solución, TIPSA / GLS ES). The text is supplied on the resolve request as `resolution_note` and is NOT echoed back on the resource.

initial_carrier_substatus_code.description: Carrier-specific sub-status code (CTT-only for now). Stores `reason` or `reason/situation` (e.g. `"11/B"`). `null` for other carriers.

allowed_resolution_options.description: Resolution options the carrier accepts for this incidence in its current state. Computed by shipping-service from `(carrier, carrier_status_code, carrier_substatus_code)`. Empty array when the carrier does not support resolution.

is_active.description:
Operational state — `true` while the carrier still reports incidence for this tracking; `false` once it was closed.

- **Automatic closure**: shipping-service flips it to `false` as soon as the package leaves `INCIDENCE` (e.g. EMG/EMI webhook after an EMH) and sets `resolved_at`. It does NOT touch `status`, `resolution_status` or `resolution_data` — the user workflow is preserved.
- **Manual change via API**: `POST /(dropshipper|admin)/issues/{id}/resolve` ONLY changes `status`, `resolution_status`, `resolution_data` (and stamps `resolution_changed_at`). It does NOT touch `is_active` or `resolved_at`.

To list what needs attention: `is_active=true`. For history closed by the carrier: `is_active=false`.

resolution_data.description: Additional payload persisted when `status == RESOLVED` and `resolution_status` is `RETRY` or `CHANGE_ADDRESS`. `null` for every other case (including PICKUP_AT_AGENCY and RETURN_REQUESTED).

resolution_changed_at.description:
Timestamp of the last `status` change made by the dropshipper / admin via API (`POST /(dropshipper|admin)/issues/{id}/resolve`). Independent of `resolved_at` (carrier closure).

- `null` while the incidence stays in `INFO` or `PENDING`.
- Set once when the incidence transitions out of `PENDING` (transitions are one-shot).

resolved_at.description: Timestamp of the automatic carrier-side closure (when `is_active` flips to `false` because of DELIVERED / OUT_FOR_DELIVERY). Manual API changes do NOT populate this field — use `resolution_changed_at` for that.

pickup_point.description: Pickup point associated with the incidence (carrier-side store / agency / locker where the package is available). Only populated when the carrier reported a pickup event that identifies the point (CTT `EMW`) and the point was synced to the catalog. In every other case (most incidences) it is `null` — the key is always present.

PickupPointDayHours.description:
Opening hours for a single day at a pickup point. The carrier
exposes up to two windows per day (morning / afternoon). Closed
windows come through as `null`.

day.description: Day of the week in lowercase (`monday`..`sunday`).

PickupPoint.description:
Pickup point (carrier-agnostic) where the recipient can collect
the package. shipping-service resolves it from the identifier
the carrier reports in the event and exposes all its fields.
Fields not provided by the carrier come through as `null`;
`hours` may be an empty array.

pup_id.description: Carrier-side identifier of the pickup point.

is_active.description: Whether the pickup point is currently operational.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last sync from the carrier catalog.

ResolutionRetry.description:
`resolution_data` payload accepted (and persisted) when
`resolution_status == RETRY`. Captures the new delivery attempt
the DP wants the carrier to make.

date.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) when the retry should be attempted.

ResolutionAddress.description:
Address sub-document for the CHANGE_ADDRESS resolution. Mirrors the
order's `shipping_address` shape: free-text `street` (including the
house number), optional `address_line_2`, plus `postal_code`,
`city`, `state` (province / region), and ISO-2 `country`.

ResolutionChangeAddress.description:
`resolution_data` payload accepted (and persisted) when
`resolution_status == CHANGE_ADDRESS`. Wraps the new address the
carrier must redirect the parcel to.

ResolveIssueInput.description:
Payload accepted by `POST /(dropshipper|admin)/issues/{id}/resolve`.

Transitions a `PENDING` issue to one of the two final user-driven
states (`MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT` or `RESOLVED`).

Combinations:
  - `status=MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT`: `resolution_status` and
    `resolution_data` MUST be absent.
  - `status=RESOLVED` + `resolution_status=RETRY`:
    `resolution_data = { date, time_window }` REQUIRED.
  - `status=RESOLVED` + `resolution_status=CHANGE_ADDRESS`:
    `resolution_data = { address: {...} }` REQUIRED.
  - `status=RESOLVED` + `resolution_status=PICKUP_AT_AGENCY`:
    `resolution_data` MUST be absent.
  - `status=RESOLVED` + `resolution_status=RETURN_REQUESTED`:
    `resolution_data` MUST be absent.
  - `status=RESOLVED` + `resolution_status=SOLUTION_PROVIDED`:
    `resolution_data` MUST be absent and `resolution_note` is REQUIRED
    (free-text solution — TIPSA / GLS ES "aportar solución").

`resolution_note` is a free-text note (max 500 chars). Optional in
general, but REQUIRED when `resolution_status = SOLUTION_PROVIDED`.
Forwarded to the carrier when it supports a resolution push (e.g.
TIPSA). It is REQUEST-ONLY: it never appears on the Issue resource
(`GET /dropshipper/issues/{id}`) nor in the `issue.resolved` webhook.

resolution_data.description:
Required iff `resolution_status` is `RETRY` (with
`date` + `time_window`) or `CHANGE_ADDRESS` (with `address`).
Forbidden otherwise.

resolution_note.description:
Optional free-text note (max 500 chars) forwarded to the carrier
for carriers that support a resolution push (e.g. TIPSA).
Request-only: never persisted, never returned on the Issue
resource or the `issue.resolved` webhook.
resolution_note.example: Cliente confirmó nueva dirección por teléfono.

id.description: Sequential `store_id` of the shop. Use this value as the `{id}` path param on `/dropshipper/shops/{id}` and related endpoints.

OperationStatus.description:
Polling response returned by `/supplier/operations/{id}` and
`/dropshipper/operations/{id}`. Reflects the cached state of the saga that
the original mutation kicked off, so clients can recover from a
504 saga-wait timeout without re-issuing the request (which would
risk a duplicate side-effect on the server).

operation_id.description: The same value as the `Idempotency-Key` you sent on the original mutation, echoed back in its 504 body — poll with the key you already have.

status.description:
- `in_progress`: the saga is still running.
- `completed`: the saga finished with a 2xx response. `result` is set.
- `failed`: the saga finished with a 4xx response. `error` is set.

result.description: Response payload of the original mutation. Only set when `status == completed`.

error.description: Failure details of the original mutation. Only set when `status == failed`.

resource.description: Best-effort pointer to the affected resource derived from the response body.

Webhook.description: Webhook subscription attached to an API Key.

topic.description:
Canonical topic the subscription is bound to. One of the
stable snake-case values listed in the Webhooks tag overview.

url.description: Destination URL where webhook payloads are POSTed.

active.description:
Whether the subscription is active. Auto-deactivated after 3
consecutive failed deliveries; re-enable from the API Keys
section of your Dropea dashboard.

topic.description:
Topic the subscription binds to. One of the dropshipper webhook
topics listed in the Webhooks tag overview. An unknown topic is
rejected with `400`.

ShopProductLinkInput.description:
Body for `POST /dropshipper/shops/{id}/products/link`. The
endpoint is shop-agnostic; the fields are resolved per `store_type`.
For SHOPIFY, `external_product_id` and (per LINK mapping)
`external_variant_id` are required and carry the Shopify GraphQL gids.
For GENERIC, only `product_id` and the `variant_id`s are used
(the `action` / external ids are ignored).

external_product_id.description:
External shop product id. Required for SHOPIFY (the Shopify
GraphQL gid `gid://shopify/Product/...`); ignored for GENERIC.

action.description:
LINK binds to an existing external variant; CREATE creates a
new external variant. Ignored for GENERIC shops.

external_variant_id.description:
External shop variant id. Required when `action=LINK` for
SHOPIFY; ignored for GENERIC.

ShopProductCreateInput.description:
Body for `POST /dropshipper/shops/{id}/products`. Creates
the whole Dropea product in the external shop (SHOPIFY only at
runtime). `product_name` / `detail` / `images` / `videos` are optional
overrides; when omitted the Dropea product's own data is used.

product_name.description: Optional override of the external product title.

detail.description: Optional override of the external product description.

ShopProductAssociation.description:
A single Dropea-product ↔ shop association, as returned by the link /
create endpoints. The Dropea product / variant are referenced by their
public sequential numbers; the external (Shopify) ids and sync status
are present only for SHOPIFY shops.

external_product_id.description: External shop product id (Shopify gid). Absent for GENERIC shops.

external_variant_id.description: External shop variant id (Shopify gid). Absent for GENERIC shops.

sync_status.description: External sync status. Absent for GENERIC shops.

external_sku.description: SKU registered in the external shop. Absent for GENERIC shops.

ShopProductLinkResult.description:
Payload returned on a settled link / create saga: the shop and the
resulting associations (public projection — no internal ids/metadata).

ShopProductUnlinkInput.description:
Body for `POST /dropshipper/shops/{id}/products/unlink`. Performs a
COMPLETE dissociation of the listed variants. Pass every variant of
the product to unlink it entirely.

variant_ids.description: Public Dropea variant identifiers (sequential) to unlink.

ShopProductUnlinkResult.description:
Payload returned on a settled unlink saga: the shop plus the product
and variants that were dissociated (echoed public sequential numbers).

variant_ids.description: Public Dropea variant identifiers that were unlinked.

tags.description: Reference lookups for the dropshipper integration (order statuses, carriers, etc.). Static enumerations meant to be fetched once and cached locally — they are not business resources, are not paginated, and do not change frequently. Use them to render dropdowns, decode codes returned by other endpoints, or seed local copies.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Subscribe one or more webhook URLs per API Key from the **API Keys** section of your Dropea dashboard to receive real-time POSTs when Dropea resources change. Each API Key holds an independent list of `(topic, URL)` pairs. ### Public topics - **`order.created`** — New order created. `resource` is modeled identically to the GET order response. - **`order.status.changed`** — Order state machine transitioned. The current state lives in `resource.status` / `resource.sub_status`. Integrators that need to detect specific transitions should cache the last seen state per `resource_id`. - **`order.cancelled`** — Order cancelled (by dropshipper, supplier or system). - **`issue.created`** — A new shipment incidence was created. **Branch on `resource.status` + `resource.is_active`**: action is required only when `status="PENDING" && is_active=true`. - **`issue.status.changed`** — The dropshipper updated the workflow status of an incidence. `resource.is_active` reflects whether the carrier still has it open. - **`issue.resolved`** — A shipment incidence was closed — typically because the carrier moved the shipment out of INCIDENCE. Each topic's payload schema is documented under **Sample payloads by topic** below, with the schema name pointing to the **Models** sidebar section for the full field reference. ### Headers sent with every delivery - `X-Dropea-Topic` — topic name (matches `topic` in the body). - `X-Dropea-Event-Id` — UUID per delivery. Store it for idempotent processing. - `X-Dropea-Signature` — `sha256=`. Verify with a constant-time comparison over the raw request body bytes. The `signing_secret` is shown ONCE when you create the API Key — it is shared by all webhook subscriptions (topics) created under that key, not regenerated per subscription — store it server-side. ### Body structure (v2 envelope) Every webhook uses the same flat envelope. Resource state lives inside `resource`, modeled byte-for-byte after the public REST representation for the same resource (e.g. `GET /dropshipper/orders/{order_number}` for order webhooks, `GET /supplier/products/{product_id}` for product webhooks). A GET of the same resource returns the same shape. - `topic` — string. Matches the `X-Dropea-Topic` header. - `market` — string. Market of the deploy that emitted the event (e.g. `"PT"`, `"ES"`, `"IT"`) — varies per deploy/market. - `event_id` — string. UUID v4, identical to `X-Dropea-Event-Id`. Use it for idempotent processing. - `event_at` — string. UTC timestamp of the event itself, ISO 8601 (`2026-05-21T14:32:11.000Z`). - `resource_id` — integer. Sequential numeric id of the resource (matches `resource.id` / `resource.product_id` / etc). - `resource` — object. Snapshot of the resource at emission time. **Status values are uppercase** (`PENDING`, `CONFIRMED.PENDING_SUPPLIER`, `FINISH.CANCELLED`, `PUBLIC`, `INACTIVE`, ...) — same enums the REST endpoints return. > The envelope does NOT carry a `previous_state` field. Integrators that need to detect specific transitions (`PROCESSING.PICKING → PROCESSING.PACKED`, etc.) should cache the last seen `resource.status` / `resource.sub_status` keyed by `resource_id` and diff on each delivery — same pattern used by Shopify and GitHub. Body keys are emitted in this order so the payload reads as a narrative: **what + where → delivery identity (id + when) → resource snapshot**. ### Sample payloads by topic Click any topic to expand its sample payload.
order.created **Schema:** `WebhookOrderCreated` — open the **Models** section in the sidebar to see the full structure with enum values for every field. ```json { "topic": "order.created", "market": "PT", "event_id": "24cdc4a3-7e0f-4d7b-bb5a-3c2af7c5b87c", "event_at": "2026-05-21T14:32:11.000Z", "resource_id": 14, "resource": { /* full Order shape — same as GET /dropshipper/orders/14 */ } } ```
order.status.changed **Schema:** `WebhookOrderStatusChanged` — open the **Models** section in the sidebar to see the full structure with enum values for every field. ```json { "topic": "order.status.changed", "market": "PT", "event_id": "0d1f7d4a-9216-4f9c-9c8b-bc1d8b9f5d2e", "event_at": "2026-05-21T14:32:11.000Z", "resource_id": 14, "resource": { /* full Order shape */ } } ```
order.cancelled **Schema:** `WebhookOrderCancelled` — open the **Models** section in the sidebar to see the full structure with enum values for every field. ```json { "topic": "order.cancelled", "market": "PT", "event_id": "2b4a9c8d-3e5f-4a1b-8c2d-7e9f1a3b5c7d", "event_at": "2026-05-21T15:11:42.000Z", "resource_id": 14, "resource": { /* full Order shape — status = FINISH, sub_status = CANCELLED */ } } ```
issue.created **Schema:** `WebhookIssueCreated` — open the **Models** section in the sidebar to see the full structure with enum values for every field. ```json { "topic": "issue.created", "market": "PT", "event_id": "3a1b2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d", "event_at": "2026-05-21T10:15:00.000Z", "resource_id": 5, "resource": { /* full Issue shape — same as the list endpoint item */ } } ```
issue.status.changed **Schema:** `WebhookIssueStatusChanged` — open the **Models** section in the sidebar to see the full structure with enum values for every field. ```json { "topic": "issue.status.changed", "market": "PT", "event_id": "9f8e7d6c-5b4a-3928-bcde-1f2e3d4c5b6a", "event_at": "2026-05-21T11:00:00.000Z", "resource_id": 5, "resource": { /* full Issue shape */ } } ```
issue.resolved **Schema:** `WebhookIssueResolved` — open the **Models** section in the sidebar to see the full structure with enum values for every field. ```json { "topic": "issue.resolved", "market": "PT", "event_id": "7e6d5c4b-3a29-4f1e-8d7c-6b5a4938271f", "event_at": "2026-05-21T15:00:00.000Z", "resource_id": 5, "resource": { /* full Issue shape — status = RESOLVED */ } } ```
### Delivery contract Reply with any `2xx` within **5 seconds**. Failures are retried with a constant `1m / 5m / 15m` backoff. After 3 consecutive failed attempts the subscription is auto-deactivated — you must re-enable it from the **API Keys** section of your Dropea dashboard.

get.description:
Returns the carriers configured in shipping-service. Each entry
exposes the public `code` (e.g. `"GLS"`, `"TIPSA"`, `"CTT"`),
the human-readable `name`, and the embedded `services` list.
Use this catalog to populate the `carrier` and `service_type`
fields when creating or updating orders — every `services[].code`
returned here is a valid `service_type` for the parent carrier.
Internal identifiers and credential snapshots are never exposed —
integrators address carriers by `code`.

Returns the documented list of order statuses the public API uses.
Each entry has a string `key` (e.g. `PENDING`), a human-readable
`label`, a `description`, and the `sub_statuses[]` collection
observable while the order is in that top-level status. Numeric
ids are not exposed — callers reference statuses by `key`
everywhere.

items.label: Processing
items.description: Supplier is picking and packing the order.

sub_statuses.label: Picking
sub_statuses.description: Supplier is picking the items from the warehouse.

sub_statuses.label: Packed
sub_statuses.description: Order is packed and ready for dispatch.

items.label: Finished
items.description: Terminal state: delivered, paid, cancelled, refused or lost/damaged.

sub_statuses.label: Delivered
sub_statuses.description: Order successfully delivered to the customer.

get.description:
Paginated listing of carrier-reported issues belonging to the
authenticated dropshipper. The owner is taken from the API Key
context and cannot be overridden via query params.

Use `status` to filter the workflow state (a CSV of `INFO`,
`PENDING`, `MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT`, `RESOLVED`). The
`resolution_changed_at_from`/`_to` range filters by the timestamp
of the last user-driven state change. The canonical use case is a
dropshipper pulling its pending issues:
`GET /dropshipper/issues?status=PENDING`.

parameters.name: is_active
parameters.description: When set, filters by whether the carrier still has the issue open (`is_active=false` means the carrier closed it). Cannot be combined with `only_pending_to_resolve`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: CSV of one or more `IssueStatus` values to filter by (`INFO`, `PENDING`, `MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT`, `RESOLVED`). Cannot be combined with `only_pending_to_resolve`.

parameters.name: only_pending_to_resolve
parameters.description: Convenience shortcut for the "issues the dropshipper still has to act on" bucket. When `true`, forces `status=PENDING` and `is_active=true`. Mutually exclusive with `status` and `is_active` (sending it alongside either yields a 400).

parameters.name: resolution_changed_at_from
parameters.description: ISO 8601 datetime. Only issues with `resolution_changed_at` greater than or equal to this value are returned.

parameters.name: resolution_changed_at_to
parameters.description: ISO 8601 datetime. Only issues with `resolution_changed_at` less than or equal to this value are returned.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Exact-match filter on the issue's `shipment_incidence_number`. When set, the response contains at most one item — the incidence carrying that id, if any. Convenience for integrators that already know the user-facing id from a previous response. Mutually exclusive with `order_number` (sending both yields a 400).

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Filter by the order's sequential numeric id (`order_number`). Returns the issues linked to that order. Like every public id this is the human-facing numeric id, not the Mongo `_id`. Mutually exclusive with `id` (sending both yields a 400).

get.summary: Get one own issue by id
get.description:
Returns a single issue belonging to the authenticated dropshipper,
identified by its user-facing `shipment_incidence_number` (the same
value surfaced as `id` in the listing). Returns 404 when the id does
not exist OR belongs to another owner — external consumers cannot
probe foreign ids.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Auto-incremental `shipment_incidence_number` of the issue.

post.description:
Move a `PENDING` issue to one of the two final user-driven states.
Only owned issues can be transitioned — the API Key owner is the
only one allowed to mutate them. INFO issues are immutable here;
MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT and RESOLVED are themselves final.

Body shape (validated by the route):

  - `status` (required) — `MANAGING_WITH_CLIENT` or `RESOLVED`.
  - `resolution_status` (required iff `status=RESOLVED`) — one of
    `RETRY`, `CHANGE_ADDRESS`, `PICKUP_AT_AGENCY`, `RETURN_REQUESTED`.
  - `resolution_data` (required iff `resolution_status` is `RETRY`
    or `CHANGE_ADDRESS`) — `{date, time_window}` or `{address}`.

The successful response stamps `resolution_changed_at` with the
current timestamp.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Auto-incremental `shipment_incidence_number` of the issue to transition. Same value returned as `id` in the listing/response payloads.

Same handler as `/supplier/operations/{operation_id}` — both rolesegments
expose the polling endpoint so each Swagger surface advertises it
to its integrators. Ownership is scoped to the polling API Key.
List orders visible to the authenticated owner, filtered by query params and paginated.

Field that `date_from` / `date_to` filter against. Defaults to
`created_at` when omitted. Use `confirmed_at` for the moment
the dropshipper confirmed the order, `processing_at` for when
it entered preparation, and `delivered_at` for the delivery
timestamp.

parameters.name: carrier
parameters.description:
Filter by carrier code. The live list of valid codes is obtained from the
**List carriers** endpoint (`GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`).

parameters.name: service_type
parameters.description:
Filter by carrier-specific service code. The valid codes are obtained from the
**List carriers** endpoint (`GET /dropshipper/catalogs/carriers`) — inspect

parameters.name: supplier_id
parameters.description: Sequential supplier number (supplier_number).

parameters.name: product_id
parameters.description: Sequential product number(s) (product_number). Accepts CSV or repeated params.

parameters.name: pack_id
parameters.description: Filter to orders containing items from any of the given bundle/pack ids. Accepts CSV or repeated params.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against `shipping_address.city`.

parameters.name: province
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against `shipping_address.state`.

parameters.name: external_order_id
parameters.description:
Exact match against the order's `store_external_order_id` (the
"Pedido Tienda" identifier persisted from Shopify, e.g. `#3305`).
The filter is bidirectional — both `#3305` and `3305` match the
same record, so callers do not need to know that Shopify stores
the value with a leading `#`.

post.description:
Creates an order **synchronously**. The endpoint publishes the
saga-initiating event on NATS and waits up to 15s for it to settle:

- **200** — the saga completed in time; the response body is the
  full created order.
- **504** — the saga did not settle within the timeout. The body
  carries an `operation_id` you can poll via
  `GET /dropshipper/operations/{operation_id}`. This
  `operation_id` is **the same value as the `Idempotency-Key`
  you sent**, so you poll with the key you already have. On a
  late success the `order.created` webhook
  also fires; if creation fails there is no dedicated webhook —
  poll the operation above instead.

Validation of the requested store and line items happens inline
before the event is published — an unknown `store_id` or line
items that span multiple suppliers surface as 400. Order-service
additionally enforces that the authenticated caller owns the
target store (see 403 below); admin-scoped keys and Shopify
webhook orders are exempt.

This endpoint requires a unique `Idempotency-Key` header — replayed
requests with the same key return the cached response.

200.description: Saga completed within timeout; returns the created order.

403.description:
Forbidden. Two scenarios return 403: the API key is missing the
`orders:create` permission, OR the authenticated caller does
not own the target store (the create is rejected with
`CREATOR_NOT_STORE_OWNER` before the saga runs).

504.description: Saga did not complete within 15s. Client should poll the operation id.

get.description: Fetch a single order visible to the authenticated owner.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sequential order number (order_number).

patch.description:
Update a mutable subset of an existing order. Honours the same sync
contract as POST (15s saga wait + 504 with `operation_id` on
timeout). `Idempotency-Key` is optional (I2266) — if omitted, the
server generates one and echoes it back for polling.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sequential order number (order_number).

200.description: Saga completed within timeout; returns the updated order.

post.description: Cancel an existing order. Honours the 15s saga-wait + 504 contract and requires an Idempotency-Key header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sequential order number (order_number).

200.description: Order cancelled successfully. Returns only the id and final status.

post.description: Move a draft/pending order into CONFIRMED. Honours the 15s saga-wait + 504 contract and requires an Idempotency-Key header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sequential order number (order_number).

200.description: Order confirmed successfully. Returns only the id and final status.

get.description: List products visible to the authenticated dropshipper. Results include only products the dropshipper can purchase — publicly listed products and exclusives where the caller has an allocation.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search over product name/description/SKU.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Narrow by visible status(es). Accepts a single value (`?status=PUBLIC`), CSV (`?status=PUBLIC,EXCLUSIVE`), or repeated params (`?status=PUBLIC&status=EXCLUSIVE`).

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Category id(s) to filter by. Accepts a single value, CSV, or repeated params.

parameters.name: suppliers
parameters.description: Supplier id(s) to filter by. Accepts CSV or repeated params.

parameters.name: supplier_id
parameters.description: Single-value alternative to `suppliers`. Pass one supplier id; equivalent to `suppliers=<value>`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Batch fetch by `product_number` (positive integers). Accepts CSV or repeated params.

get.description: Fetch a single product by its sequential `product_number`. Returns 404 when the product does not exist or the caller is not allowed to see it (dropshippers only see PUBLIC products and EXCLUSIVE products with allocation).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sequential product number (positive integer).

get.description: List shops visible to the authenticated owner.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Free-text search over shop name/URL/domain (maps to the downstream `search` field).

parameters.name: dropshipper
parameters.description: Admin-only: narrow by dropshipper id(s). Accepts CSV or repeated params.

post.summary: Create a Dropea product in a shop
post.description:
Create the whole Dropea product (with the listed variants) in the
merchant's external shop. The endpoint is shop-agnostic: it
resolves the shop and dispatches by `store_type`. Only **SHOPIFY**
is supported at runtime — a GENERIC / WOOCOMMERCE / UNKNOWN shop
returns `422 STORE_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED`.

`product_name`, `detail`, `images` and `videos` are OPTIONAL
overrides — when omitted the Dropea product's own name, description
and media are used. The product and variants are referenced by their
public sequential numbers.

Asynchronous: 201 on a settled saga, 504 + `operation_id` on timeout.
`Idempotency-Key` is optional (I2266) — if omitted, the server
generates one and echoes it back.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sequential shop number.

201.description: Product created in the shop. Saga completed within the budget.

422.description:
Unprocessable. Returned with code `STORE_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED` when
the resolved shop type does not support product creation
(GENERIC / WOOCOMMERCE / UNKNOWN), or for other validation
failures.

504.description: Saga did not complete within the budget. Poll the operation id.

post.summary: Link a Dropea product to a shop
post.description:
Link a Dropea product to the merchant's shop. The endpoint is
shop-agnostic: it resolves the shop and dispatches by `store_type`.

- **SHOPIFY**: `external_product_id` and `variant_mapping` are
  required. Each mapping either LINKs the Dropea variant to an
  existing Shopify variant (`action=LINK`, `external_variant_id`
  required — its SKU and price are overwritten with the Dropea
  values) or CREATEs a new Shopify variant (`action=CREATE`). The
  external ids are the Shopify GraphQL gids (`gid://shopify/Product/...`,
  `gid://shopify/ProductVariant/...`).
- **GENERIC**: only `product_id` and the `variant_id`s of the
  `variant_mapping` are used (the `action` / external ids are
  ignored). The Dropea product + variants are associated to the shop.
- **WOOCOMMERCE / UNKNOWN**: `422 STORE_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED`.

The Dropea product and variants are referenced by their public
sequential numbers; they are resolved to internal ids BEFORE any saga
is fired (unknown numbers return 404/400 with no side effect).

Asynchronous: a settled saga returns 201 with the created
associations; if it does not settle within the budget the response
is 504 with an `operation_id` to poll. `Idempotency-Key` is optional
(I2266) — if omitted, the server generates one and echoes it back.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Sequential shop number.

201.description: Product linked. Saga completed within the budget.

422.description:
Unprocessable. Returned with code `STORE_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED` when
the resolved shop type does not support the link operation
(WOOCOMMERCE / UNKNOWN), or for other validation failures.

504.description: Saga did not complete within the budget. Poll the operation id.

post.summary: Unlink a Dropea product from a shop
post.description:
Unlink (dissociate) a Dropea product from the merchant's shop. The
endpoint is shop-agnostic and performs a COMPLETE dissociation — the
shop-product association of each listed variant is removed (soft
delete); for SHOPIFY the variants are also unlinked from the external
shop. SHOPIFY and GENERIC shops are supported; a WOOCOMMERCE / UNKNOWN
shop returns `422 STORE_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED`.

The product and variants are referenced by their public sequential
numbers and resolved to internal ids BEFORE any saga is fired (unknown
numbers return 404/400 with no side effect). Pass every variant of the
product to unlink it entirely.

Asynchronous: a settled saga returns 200 echoing the unlinked ids; if
it does not settle within the budget the response is 504 with an
`operation_id` to poll. `Idempotency-Key` is optional (I2266) — if
omitted, the server generates one and echoes it back.

422.description:

(WOOCOMMERCE / UNKNOWN), or for other validation failures.

get.summary: List webhook subscriptions of the calling API Key
get.description:
Returns the webhook subscriptions attached to the API Key
authenticating the request.

post.description:
Register a webhook URL on the calling API Key. Used by
integrations (e.g. ChatBy) to receive Dropea-side events.

`Idempotency-Key` is optional (I2266) — if sent, replays within
24 h return the cached response with `Idempotent-Replay: true`; if
omitted, the server generates one and echoes it back.

delete.description:
Remove a webhook subscription from the calling API Key.
`Idempotency-Key` is optional (I2266) — but — unlike the mutating
`POST`/`PATCH`/`PUT` endpoints — `DELETE` is naturally idempotent:
there is no cached replay (no `Idempotent-Replay` header, no 409
on a concurrent retry). Retrying simply re-runs the delete and is
always safe.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Webhook subscription id.
